Chari Kelly

Democratic candidate for Supreme Court, Place 2 (unexpired term), Texas

Justice, Texas Third Court of Appeals (Austin)

Chari Kelly is a Democrat who has served as a justice on the Texas Third Court of Appeals in Austin since 2019. She ran unopposed in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary for Texas Supreme Court Place 2 and won with 1,880,663 votes. In the November 3, 2026 general election she faces Republican Justice James P. Sullivan, whom Gov. Greg Abbott appointed to the seat in 2025.

Where Kelly stands

Judicial independence
Says Texas needs a Supreme Court that is independent of political pressure and willing to enforce the law even when powerful people or institutions are involved.
Limits on government power
Points to her appellate rulings that the Attorney General was not above the law in a whistleblower case and that the governor lacks absolute authority under the Texas Disaster Act. She says these rulings are not promises about future cases.
Balance on the Court
Notes that eight of the nine current justices first joined the Court by appointment from a Republican governor. Argues that voters should value balance and independence on the Court.
Access to justice
Says Supreme Court decisions shape whether Texans can meaningfully get into court, and stresses the Court's role in running the judicial system and in public confidence that it is fair.
Qualifications and experience
Says her trial, appellate, government, defense and teaching experience gives her a broad view of Texas law. She cites more than 800 opinions she has written and her board certification in Judicial Administration.
Representation of women on the Court
Notes that Texas has never had a full-time elected female majority on its Supreme Court and calls 2026 a historic opportunity to elect qualified women.

Background

  • Justice, Texas Third Court of Appeals, Place 3 (2019–present)
  • U.S. Army JAG Captain and paratrooper; trial defense counsel (2003–2007, per Ballotpedia)
  • Assistant District Attorney, prosecuting felony cases in Comal and Travis counties
  • Texas Assistant Attorney General, Medicaid fraud litigation
  • Has taught trial advocacy at the University of Texas School of Law for nearly 20 years
  • Past president, Austin Bar Association and Austin Young Lawyers Association; past chair, Austin Bar Foundation
  • Board certified in Judicial Administration and in Criminal Law
  • Education: B.A., University of Florida; J.D., University of Texas at Austin
